A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diagram-understanding evaluation study. All 51 pages of v1 and 49 pages of v2, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, tables and figures that can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of GPT-4V, GPT-4o and Gemini on synthetic and real diagrams, including accuracy tables, robustness analyses and model-response case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of three open models and a GPT-4o experiment using instructions to ignore prior knowledge.

M1.justification: The graph-based diagram construction, question taxonomy and knowledge-grounding procedure remain unchanged. The new system prompt is tested as an experimental control; no replacement algorithm, model architecture or proposed inference method is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic diagram tasks and 1,001 FoodWeb/AI2D diagrams across six scientific domains. Dataset statistics match between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 8, and Appendix D retains the domain-specific annotations. Added models and prompt controls use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds LLaMA-3.2-11B-Vision, LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Qwen2-VL-7B alongside GPT-4V, GPT-4o and Gemini. These additions substantially broaden the actual comparisons across main CoT evaluations, zero-shot results and the appendix spatial-position evaluation.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3.1 adds a controlled GPT-4o CoT comparison using an instruction to ignore prior knowledge. The added models also extend evaluation to specified 7B/11B configurations. Existing accuracy metrics, question formats, zero-shot/CoT conditions, four-shot ICL and arrow-variation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a prompt-sensitivity experiment testing whether instructing GPT-4o to ignore prior knowledge changes accuracy, and extends the existing spatial-position diagnostic to three additional models. Arrow-variation tests, ICL tests, complexity analyses and the modified-foodweb case study are retained.

E5.justification: The GPT seed statements in Appendix E.1 remain unchanged. Both versions report point accuracies and model averages without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests; the added results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive scores for three models, revised model-set averages and Figure 8's prompt-control results. For example, Table 2 adds LLaVA text-entity recognition/counting accuracies of 38.9%/26.6%. Most original-model scores are retained after rounding. Gemini's semantic-recognition gain is corrected from 6.37 to 3.7 percentage points between v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: The graph representation, entity/relation definitions and question-set formalization remain unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of strong entity handling, weak relational understanding and knowledge shortcuts explaining apparent diagram competence. The expanded model evaluation does not redefine the main contribution or these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds qualifications for LLaVA's different responses to knowledge-required questions and speculates that model weakness explains its negligible relation-recognition benefit. Appendix B newly identifies simple prompts and answer parsers as limitations that future work could improve.

D1.justification: v2 adds a HuggingFace data/annotation link, diagram-filtering details and the exact no-prior system message. However, Appendix E.1 still documents only the original three models. The uniform-sampling footnote and explicit 885-diagram semantic-subset count disappear; this does not establish that sampling actually changed.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds focused discussion of chart and flowchart understanding, including ChartQA, FlowVQA and FlowLearn, and positions the knowledge-shortcut investigation against this work. Citations for the newly evaluated models and additional benchmarks are added while the existing research framing is largely retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions and explanatory additions, introduces appendix subsections, changes author order and removes the equal-contribution note. The main argument and section sequence remain stable. Table 1 corrects the swapped examples for real-entity recognition and counting.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from one to two columns, and the appendices are substantially reflowed. Main tables are rebuilt around CoT results, zero-shot results are consolidated into Table 9, dataset statistics move to Appendix D, and a new prompt-comparison Figure 8 is added. Existing illustrations and example panels are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The open-model comparisons broaden evidence beyond v1's three proprietary models, while the prompt control tests instruction sensitivity and the data link improves access information. These provide a modest net gain. Integration remains incomplete: LLaVA's low entity scores conflict with retained near-perfect-entity claims, Table 11 keeps old three-model summaries, and Appendix E.1 lacks configurations for the added models.
